definitions.definition: A voluntary undertaking is a commitment accepted by the Data Protection Board of India from any person, at any stage of a proceeding under section 28, in respect of any matter related to observance of the provisions of this Act, which may include an undertaking to take or refrain from taking specified action within a determined time, and or publicising such undertaking, acceptance of which bars further proceedings under the Act as regards the contents of the undertaking, provided the terms are adhered to.
definitions.plain_english: A voluntary undertaking is a formal promise made by a company or individual to the Data Protection Board, agreeing to do something (like fix a data breach issue) or stop doing something (like misusing personal data) within a set time. Once the Board accepts this promise, it acts like a settlement — the Board cannot take further legal action against that person for the same issue as long as they keep their promise. If the person breaks the promise, it is treated as breaking the law itself, and the Board can then impose penalties.
real_world_examples: A major Indian e-commerce platform like Flipkart, under investigation by the Data Protection Board for failing to implement adequate data security measures, offers a voluntary undertaking to deploy end-to-end encryption and conduct a data audit within six months, thereby halting the formal inquiry proceedings.

A health-tech startup based in Bengaluru, accused of sharing users' sensitive medical records with third-party advertisers without consent, voluntarily undertakes to immediately cease the data-sharing practice, notify affected Data Principals, and publicise a corrective action plan on its website.

A large Indian bank under proceedings for not honouring Data Principals' requests to erase their personal data submits a voluntary undertaking to the Board, committing to build and deploy an automated erasure mechanism within ninety days, with the Board's consent to extend the timeline by thirty days after mutual agreement.

An EdTech company processing children's data without verifiable parental consent offers a voluntary undertaking to the Board to suspend data collection from users below eighteen years of age and redesign its consent mechanism, preventing the Board from imposing financial penalties for the duration of compliance.

A telecom company like Airtel, facing a proceeding for a large-scale personal data breach, proactively approaches the Board and undertakes to notify all affected users, engage an independent cybersecurity auditor, and publicise the remediation steps taken, in exchange for a bar on further penalty proceedings related to that specific breach.
what_it_covers: A commitment by a Data Fiduciary to take affirmative corrective action (e.g., implementing security safeguards) within a Board-determined timeframe during an ongoing proceeding under section 28.
An undertaking by a person to refrain from a specific data processing activity (e.g., ceasing unauthorised sharing of personal data with third parties) as a condition accepted by the Board.
The public disclosure or publicisation of the voluntary undertaking itself, where the Board determines that transparency serves the interests of Data Principals and the public.
Modification of the terms of an already-accepted voluntary undertaking, with the mutual consent of both the Board and the person who gave the undertaking.

Situations where a person breaches the accepted voluntary undertaking, which is then deemed a breach of the Act itself, enabling the Board to proceed under section 33 after giving the person a hearing.
what_it_excludes: Undertakings offered after the Board has already concluded proceedings and passed a final order under section 33 — the voluntary undertaking mechanism is available only during a proceeding under section 28.
Unilateral internal compliance policies or self-declarations by a Data Fiduciary that have not been formally submitted to and accepted by the Data Protection Board of India.

Criminal proceedings or offences under other laws (such as the Indian Penal Code or IT Act) arising from the same facts — the bar on proceedings applies only to matters under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.
Matters outside the contents of the accepted voluntary undertaking — the Board retains full authority to proceed against the person for any aspect of non-compliance not covered by the undertaking.
Situations where the Board declines to accept the offered undertaking — the bar on proceedings only activates upon formal acceptance by the Board.
definitions.why_it_matters: Acceptance of a voluntary undertaking by the Board creates a statutory bar on further proceedings under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 in respect of the subject matter of the undertaking, effectively replacing enforcement action with a compliance commitment and preventing imposition of financial penalties under section 33. Conversely, failure to adhere to the undertaking's terms is deemed a direct breach of the Act, exposing the person to the full penalty regime under section 33, making the voluntary undertaking a high-stakes regulatory instrument.
